kicker: Functional Gradient Descent with Adaptive Representations

scenes.headline: Gradient descent on the function, not the weights
scenes.sub: Refine the stored gradient until each step is safe
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tuppence! This paper runs gradient descent on the function itself, and fixes what made that hard.

scenes.text: Store the functional gradient coarsely, certify a bound on the storage error, and refine until that bound is a fixed fraction of the gradient.
scenes.mark: refine until that bound is a fixed fraction of the gradient
scenes.say: The idea: keep a rough copy of the gradient, bound its error, and refine until that error is small next to the step.

scenes.title: Two places to take a step

left.title: Parameter space
items: Step the weights of a network
The representation is fixed up front
left.say: The usual way steps the weights, and a convex loss stops being convex.

right.title: Function space
items: Step the function along its gradient
But the gradient is a whole function
right.say: Stepping the function keeps convex losses convex. But the gradient is a whole function, too big to store.

scenes.title: One step, with a refinement loop

steps.say: Store the current function's gradient coarsely, on a few cells.
Bound how far that copy can be from the true gradient, using how steep the target gets in each cell.
If the bound is too big next to the stored gradient, split the worst cells and check again.
Once the test passes, step the function, and repeat.

parts.note: certified upper bound on the storage error
size of the stored gradient, computed exactly
parts.say: The stored gradient's size is exact.

parts.note: tolerance: 0.5 keeps the error under a third
parts.say: At epsilon one half, the relative error stays under a third.

steps.say: In the paper's toy fit, the adaptive run starts blocky and sharpens.
Fixed grids stall at their own floors; the adaptive curve keeps falling.

scenes.title: Cross-entropy test loss, kernel regression
scenes.note: lower is better; one run each
scenes.say: The adaptive run has the lowest test loss, but the network beats a depth eight fixed tree.

scenes.text: A fixed approximation caps the loss. A certified, refining one only costs memory, and the memory grows as the loss falls.

recap: Step the function, not the weights
Bound the error of the stored gradient
Refine until that error is a small fraction
scenes.say: To recap: step the function, bound what you store, and refine until the error is small.
